ui_bugs.issue: Manual character-by-character typing of 'WDL-DEMO-2026-LOVE' yields 'WDL-WDLD-EMO2-026L'. The single-strip `startsWith('WDL') ? slice(3) : clean` on line 13 was NOT converted to a while-loop as the problem statement claimed. When the controlled value already contains 'WDL-' and the user types W then D then L, the cleaned buffer becomes 'WDLWDL' and slice(3) leaves the second 'WDL' intact, corrupting the token. Paste works because the incoming value replaces the buffer entirely.

action_items: In /app/frontend/src/pages/Activate.jsx line 13, replace the single-strip with a while-loop OR mask-input approach. Suggested minimal fix: `let b = clean; while (b.startsWith('WDL')) b = b.slice(3);` — this handles the double-WDL case created by controlled-input re-feed. Note: this will swallow a user's intentionally-typed 'WDL' after the prefix, but for the specified sandbox token 'WDL-DEMO-2026-LOVE' (where user content is DEMO2026LOVE) this produces the correct output. A more robust fix is to only format the substring AFTER position 4 (past the fixed 'WDL-' prefix).

rca of the issue: formatToken(v) reads the ENTIRE controlled input value on every keystroke. When state='WDL-' and user presses 'W', React calls onChange with 'WDL-W'. formatToken cleans to 'WDLW', sees the WDL prefix and slices once → 'W', producing 'WDL-W'. That's fine. But at the third char, state='WDL-WD' and user presses 'L': input='WDL-WDL', cleaned='WDLWDL', single slice(3)='WDL', joined result='WDL-WDL'. Now the user's 'WDL' becomes real content. Subsequent typed chars are appended AFTER this ghost 'WDL', producing 'WDL-WDLD-EMO2-026L' for the target 'WDL-DEMO-2026-LOVE'. Fix: while-strip in formatToken OR restrict editing to characters after the fixed 4-char 'WDL-' mask.
